title: HTMLElement: inert property - Web APIs | MDN
summary: The HTMLElement property inert reflects the value of the element's inert attribute. It is a boolean value that, when present, makes the browser "ignore" user input events for the element, including focus events and events from assistive technologies. The browser may also ignore page search and text selection in the element. This can be useful when building UIs such as modals where you would want to "trap" the focus inside the modal when it's visible.

title: aspect-ratio CSS property - CSS | MDN

This means that even if the parent container or viewport size changes, the browser will adjust the element's dimensions to maintain the specified width-to-height ratio. The specified aspect ratio is used in the calculation of auto sizes and some other layout functions.

title: Afronik Nko Font
summary: Afronik N'ko font is a display font supporting only the N'ko alphabet used to write Manding languages of West Africa Afronik N'ko font is a display font supporting only the N'ko alphabet used to write Manding languages of West Africa. Souleymane Kant created the NKo - N'Ko alphabet in 1949 to suit the sounds of the Mande languages including Mandika, Dyula, Bambara and related languages.Neither the Latin nor the Arabic characters have enough breadth to encompass the nuances of African speech. Both writing systems lack symbols for some of the phonology, in particular the subtle but distinct tonalities. When transcribed with the foreign scripts, which have no adequate way of marking precise vowel tones, the meanings of words can become confused.

title: Web Technologies Evangelist, Safari & WebKit - Careers at Apple | Jen Simmons
summary: I’m getting exciting about hiring another person to join my team at Apple, as a Web Developer Advocate on the Safari/WebKit team. The team I’m on is incredible. High impact, low stress, and we fun while we do the work. If you are interested in applying, here’s my advice: 1. Read the whole job description. The first list (Minimum Qualifications) is qualities we are looking for in every candidate. The second list (Preferred Qualifications) are the bonus qualities that could make you stand out, so if you have a few of these, you are extra interesting to us. 2. Be sure to include information on your résumé that shows us the qualities you have that match up with this list. What speaking or teaching have you done? Writing? Link to the best articles you’ve written about web technology. Building an audience on social media? What else? List relevant experience that shows why you would be a good fit for *this* role. Don’t *only* list the job roles you’ve had writing code; then we won’t know anything about you beyond that work & you won’t been seen as qualified. Your résumé will be read by a human. And since this job’s all about communicating complex ideas is a fun and simple way to understand — think about the document as a way to communicate your story about why you want this job! Show us you know how to communicate, how to decide how to tell the best story. The most frequently asked question: Where will our new hire work? The role is defined for someone to join our team at Apple Park in Cupertino, CA. (Which, but the way, is a gorgeous campus.) We *might* be able to work out something else out for an exception candidate. If you believe you are exceptional, you cannot or don’t want to move, and you’d like to talk to us anyway, knowing might be Cupertino only — do still apply. We’d love to talk to you!

linked_urls.title: Lipid nanoparticles for mRNA delivery | Nature Reviews Materials
linked_urls.summary: Messenger RNA (mRNA) has emerged as a new category of therapeutic agent to prevent and treat various diseases. To function in vivo, mRNA requires safe, effective and stable delivery systems that protect the nucleic acid from degradation and that allow cellular uptake and mRNA release. Lipid nanoparticles have successfully entered the clinic for the delivery of mRNA; in particular, lipid nanoparticle–mRNA vaccines are now in clinical use against coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), which marks a milestone for mRNA therapeutics. In this Review, we discuss the design of lipid nanoparticles for mRNA delivery and examine physiological barriers and possible administration routes for lipid nanoparticle–mRNA systems. We then consider key points for the clinical translation of lipid nanoparticle–mRNA formulations, including good manufacturing practice, stability, storage and safety, and highlight preclinical and clinical studies of lipid nanoparticle–mRNA therapeutics for infectious diseases, cancer and genetic disorders. Finally, we give an outlook to future possibilities and remaining challenges for this promising technology. Lipid nanoparticle–mRNA formulations have entered the clinic as coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccines, marking an important milestone for mRNA therapeutics. This Review discusses lipid nanoparticle design for mRNA delivery, highlighting key points for clinical translation and preclinical studies of lipid nanoparticle–mRNA therapeutics for various diseases.

summary:
Graded Exercise Therapy (#GET), once recommended as "treatment" for patients with #MECFS, has been found in multiple studies to instead cause patients *significant* harm. Thread ⬇️ graphics by Body Politic Vice Pres. Lauren Nichols:
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/FJvAnuuXEAcGy-a.jpg

linked_urls.summary: laurenthemedium on January 28, 2021: "I know many can’t relate, but I need you to know that you’ve been lucky to walk/run/yoga your way out of illness. I - and many others - need you to know that that experience isn’t one-size-fits-all, and that some illnesses worsen as a result of exertion. That exercising long enough (the GET pillar) is only beneficial to those who aren’t afflicted with an exertion disease, such as #mecfs and #longcovid. It seems counterintuitive that the thing keeping us physically and mentally healthy can exacerbate symptoms in others. It goes against what we’ve been conditioned to know, but such is the reality of a society entwined with ableism and unaware of its dangers and false narratives. I write this in response to the @bmj_company piece written by a former long hauler who used their privilege and ableism to spew falsehoods about the role of exercise in “curing” long covid. I write this with disappointment that a person who once stood in solidarity has put forth a narrative that could set the chronic illness community back by decades. Someone that I would call a “fair weather advocate”, advocating for chronic illness while it effected them, and then shitting on the community and its years of work when they no longer felt ill. On decades of experiences faced by others. And this isn’t ok. And not because of their character, but due to their lack of realizing their ableism, which (when vocalized on a large platform) perpetuates more ableism upon readers unfamiliar with the science. So I write this for healthy folx wanting to be informed, and for #longhaulers who don’t recognize their own ableism telling them that exercise cures (even though it doesn’t always). If you search for “cfs #gradedexercisetherapy ” you’ll find studies (from the CDC, the NIH, etc.) detailing why this “treatment” isn’t even controversial: it’s just wrong and not medically sound. So I encourage you to share because there are many new to chronic illness thanks to Covid. Many who think exercising long enough helps. And it can help to negate damage done by an article written by a person who doesn’t care to help a community that once welcomed and helped him and even gave him a platform.".

linked_urls.title: Getting Started With CSS Cascade Layers — Smashing Magazine
linked_urls.summary: We all have run into CSS collisions and sudden regressions in our codebases when new styles are written or 3rd-party styles are added. This is because of the interdependence of styles due to source order, specificity, and inheritance. Some ways to control the cascade have included methodologies like ITCSS and BEM and other newer native features. Cascade layers will be the ultimate native solution for resolving conflicts between multiple sources of styles. Cascade layers introduce the new at-rule of @layer. The intent is to help CSS authors be more intentional about ordering the “layers” of CSS rules as a new method of cascade management.

linked_urls.title: HTMLElement: inert property - Web APIs | MDN
linked_urls.summary: The HTMLElement property inert reflects the value of the element's inert attribute. It is a boolean value that, when present, makes the browser "ignore" user input events for the element, including focus events and events from assistive technologies. The browser may also ignore page search and text selection in the element. This can be useful when building UIs such as modals where you would want to "trap" the focus inside the modal when it's visible.

title: @jensimmons
summary: Animation improvements in Safari 16 — support for CSS Offset Path (also called Motion Path), so you can animate an object along a custom path of any shape. Plus the ability to animate changes to CSS Grid track sizes. And support for composite operations.

title: @jensimmons
summary: Overscroll Behavior support is coming to Safari 16. It determines what happens when a user scrolls inside a box and hits the end, does the rest of the page scroll or not? Useful for stopping scroll chaining.

title: @jensimmons
summary: Safari 16 adds support for Shared Worker. It runs JavaScript in the background, similar to Service Worker, but runs as long as the user has any tab open to your domain. All the tabs open to the same domain can share the same Shared Worker.

I hope to dethrone the dogma around Multi-Factor Authentication. MFA/2FA is sometimes a means to phishing-resistance, but not an end to itself.
Our industry needs friendly-to-humans, phishing-resistant, secure-by-design authentication.
Passkeys deliver this.

There are 2 types of MFA:
1. Legacy (SMS, authenticator, push) that stop some attacks, but are still susceptible to phishing
2. FIDO authentication, which is phishing resistant
MFA bypass attacks using phishing are on the rise. Migrate to FIDO authentication *this year*.

title: Jen Simmons (@jensimmons)
summary:
What I’m beginning to piece together from the most recent research goes something like this:
• SARS-CoV-2 is not like the flu or the most common coronavirus, a cold, at all.
• the initial flu-like illness is not the disease. It’s a herald — like the canker sore that shows as the first sign of syphilis
• the flu-like illness signals the *beginning* of a disease process
• as with syphilis, this initial ‘signal’ may be severe, mild, quick to heal or even asymptomatic. The severity of the herald signal says nothing about the severity of the disease process it heralds.
• the disease process is an immune destroying one. A slow, relentless attack on T-cells assures the gradual shredding of the immune system, rendering it more & more ineffective over time.
• the first sufferers to SHOW this disease process are those with existing autoimmune disorder already in progress. Many of these people (diabetics, asthmatics, other immune sufferers) die when their already overreactive immune systems go ‘apeshit’ at the virus (cytokine storms, etc)
• those with immune disturbance (ME/CFS, EDS, Crohn’s, Lupus, Sjogren’s, etc)who survive the herald illness become ‘Walking (or Bedridden) Battlegrounds’, with the primed, dysfunctional immune system fighting a losing battle with increasingly disabled T-cells.
• there are other factors (seemingly genetic…A- blood amongst others?) that make some people susceptible to this horrific process beginning about a month after the ‘herald illness’
• we say these people are suffering from ‘longcovid’
• but EVERYONE who has had a SARS-CoV-2 infection is host to the ongoing disease process — the slow dismantling of the immune system; it’s just that in some it doesn’t ‘show’ — either because it’s milder or slower, or needs a ‘trigger’ to ramp it up — or because of *where* it begins —- like the brain for instance
• we may yet discover that some people have natural immunity to SARS-CoV-2, as we discovered (eventually) with HIV;
• we may discover that some people have immune systems that do in fact successfully fight the virus off. These seem extremely rare if they exist.
This goes some way toward explaining why some some people get ‘longcovid’ on their first infection (as I did), and for some, it’s only after 2,3 or 4 infections that the ‘immune dissassembly’ part of the illness begins to show.
Only when we recognise SARS-CoV-2 as a long-term, chronic illness that sequentially disables a person (like HIV/AIDS or syphilis), will we be able to devise effective treatments.
Even were the world to STOP pushing away the truth accumulating in the research…and begin to work on the issue NOW, anything effective might be ten years away.
I will, undoubtedly, be dead by then.
I apologise to the virologists, epidemiologists, immunologists & esteemed doctors & researchers all over the world I may have insulted by putting forward my clumsy, wildly oversimplified understanding.
It’s the draft understanding of a layperson who has struggled for 30 yrs to understand & manage her SLE. 🙏🏼

linked_urls.title: Web technologies evangelist safari webkit
Web Technologies Evangelist, Safari & WebKit - Careers at Apple | Jen Simmons
linked_urls.summary: I’m getting exciting about hiring another person to join my team at Apple, as a Web Developer Advocate on the Safari/WebKit team. The team I’m on is incredible. High impact, low stress, and we fun while we do the work. If you are interested in applying, here’s my advice: 1. Read the whole job description. The first list (Minimum Qualifications) is qualities we are looking for in every candidate. The second list (Preferred Qualifications) are the bonus qualities that could make you stand out, so if you have a few of these, you are extra interesting to us. 2. Be sure to include information on your résumé that shows us the qualities you have that match up with this list. What speaking or teaching have you done? Writing? Link to the best articles you’ve written about web technology. Building an audience on social media? What else? List relevant experience that shows why you would be a good fit for *this* role. Don’t *only* list the job roles you’ve had writing code; then we won’t know anything about you beyond that work & you won’t been seen as qualified. Your résumé will be read by a human. And since this job’s all about communicating complex ideas is a fun and simple way to understand — think about the document as a way to communicate your story about why you want this job! Show us you know how to communicate, how to decide how to tell the best story. The most frequently asked question: Where will our new hire work? The role is defined for someone to join our team at Apple Park in Cupertino, CA. (Which, but the way, is a gorgeous campus.) We *might* be able to work out something else out for an exception candidate. If you believe you are exceptional, you cannot or don’t want to move, and you’d like to talk to us anyway, knowing might be Cupertino only — do still apply. We’d love to talk to you!
